three/two: In attention over the encoder, each encoder state did two jobs. It was scored against the decoder's state, and it was what got averaged.
three/split: Queries, keys and values give every token, x, three separate vectors: one to ask with, one to be scored by, and one to be mixed. Each comes from its own matrix.
three/query: The query, q, is W Q times x: what this token is looking for. With x equal to two and one, q is three and one.
three/key: The key, k, is W K times x: what this token offers to a query that comes looking. Here, two and one.
three/value: The value, v, is W V times x: what this token hands over when it is chosen. Here, one and four.
three/shape: Each matrix has one row per entry of what it makes, and one column per entry of x. With tokens of five hundred twelve numbers and queries of sixty four, W Q is sixty four by five hundred twelve.
match/ask: Now three tokens: cats, like and fish. Token two, fish, asks with its query: one and one.
match/score: Its query is scored against every token's key, its own included, with a dot product: two, zero and one.
match/weights: Softmax turns the scores into weights: zero point six seven, zero point zero nine and zero point two four.
match/mix: Fish's output is the weighted sum of the values, mostly the value of cats, two and zero. It comes to one point five eight and zero point four two.
match/roles: So the keys decide how much each token counts, and the values decide what it brings. The three matrices are learned, and every token uses the same three.
